topic: 3 drawing guidance: KATIB hardware (permanent magnet on a 2-DOF parallel robot under the writing surface)
citation: Korres G, Eid M (2020) KATIB: Haptic-Visual Guidance for Handwriting. In: Haptics: Science, Technology, Applications (EuroHaptics 2020), Springer LNCS, chapter 10.1007/978-3-030-58147-3_31 (author copy read; page numbers not checked)
task_or_setup: Stylus with stacked NdFeB N42 magnets (5 x 5 mm and 2 x 2 mm) over a 4 mm resistive touchscreen; N42 5 x 5 mm magnet on the end effector of a 2-DOF parallel manipulator (two NEMA17 steppers with 5:1 planetary gearboxes, uStepper: ATmega328 + Trinamic TMC5130 + Broadcom AEAT8800-Q24 encoder, 1800 Hz); the end-effector magnet is rotated 180 deg by a geared micro DC motor to switch the force on or off; ANSYS magnetostatics
participants_or_bench: bench demonstrations; no participants in this paper
key_quantitative_findings: Workspace 80 x 60 mm (arms 100 mm, +/-45 deg per motor); peak tangential force 0.43 N at 2-5 mm displacement (maximum around 3.5 mm) through 4 mm glass (ANSYS); stylus tilt up to 40 deg from the normal 'would result in a negligible tangential force' (as written); full-guidance playback RMS error 2.73 mm; guidance rendered at 1800 Hz.
units_and_conditions: N, mm, Hz; simulation for forces
limitations: Forces simulated, not measured; small workspace; the meaning of the tilt statement is ambiguous in the text.
relevance_to_design: Closest prior build of a permanent-magnet carriage under a writing surface; stepper-driven, quiet drivers
transferability_reason: Same physical principle and part classes
design_implication: A permanent-magnet head on a stepper stage is buildable and gives ~0.4 N through 4 mm; our heel magnet and thinner cover give more (CALC)
search_query: WebSearch Korres Eid KATIB patent contactless magnetic haptic handwriting; WebFetch author PDF

topic: Research planar haptic device (five-bar): Pantograph Mk-II
citation: Campion G, Wang Q, Hayward V (2005) The Pantograph Mk-II: a haptic instrument. Proc. IEEE/RSJ IROS 2005, pp. 723-728
task_or_setup: Two-DOF five-bar parallel mechanism, link lengths [63 75 75 63 25] mm, two Maxon RE-25 coreless DC motors (graphite brushes), optical encoders (65 536 CPR class), Quanser Q4 card; frequency response with an accelerometer
key_quantitative_findings: Workspace about 66 x 104 mm (figure); accurate tactile signals DC-400 Hz; flat response 40-300 Hz; resolves displacements of the order of 10 um (5-6 encoder ticks per 50 um); structural resonance 400-500 Hz; bearing backlash of several ticks when unloaded.
locator: Abstract; Sections II (components), III (kinematics), IV (Figs. 7-8), V
limitations: Small finger-pad device; no force values extracted; not tied to a pen.
relevance_to_design: Shows the bandwidth and resolution a direct-drive five-bar reaches (option iii)
transferability_reason: Linkage class matches; our workspace is 2-4x larger
design_implication: A pen-scale pantograph can be stiff and fast; the cost is tethering and a linkage beside the hand

topic: Electromagnet array under a tabletop acting on a magnet on the hand (option ii): FingerFlux
citation: Weiss M, Wacharamanotham C, Voelker S, Borchers J (2011) FingerFlux: near-surface haptic feedback on tabletops. Proc. UIST '11 (Santa Barbara), ACM
task_or_setup: Madgets table: 19 x 12 grid of electromagnets (19.5 mm dia x 34.5 mm, 3500 turns on iron cores) driven at 40 V DC and 255 mA, individually controllable polarity and strength, under an LCD; permanent magnets (10 mm dia x 2 mm) taped to the fingertip
key_quantitative_findings: Users felt vibration patterns up to 35 mm above the table; haptic feedback significantly reduced drifting when operating buttons without looking; electrical input per magnet 40 V x 0.255 A = 10.2 W (CALC from the paper's values).
limitations: Forces not reported in the text read; finger magnet, not a pen; iron-core grid is heavy and hot.
relevance_to_design: Evidence that a coil grid can be felt, and of its power cost (option ii)
transferability_reason: Different effector and purpose; no force data
design_implication: A no-moving-parts coil grid would need ~165 channels at ~10 W each for A4: not chosen
search_query: WebSearch FingerFlux Weiss 2011; curl RWTH PDF

topic: Electromagnetic attraction of a stylus tip that varies with position (Microsoft)
citation: Microsoft Technology Licensing LLC (inventors Autio H. A., Majander K. M.). Haptic interaction via magnetic force. US 11,036,326 B2, granted 2021-06-15; filed 2019-07-02. Status: Active, expires 2039-07-10 (as displayed on Google Patents on 2026-09-28; not verified in official register).
task_or_setup: Touch-screen device with a position sensor for a magnetically attractable stylus tip, an electromagnetic circuit whose attraction force is proportional to its current, and a drive circuit that varies the current with a haptic-force signal (e.g. variable friction/resistance); permanent-magnet tip and reversed current (repulsion) in embodiments
key_quantitative_findings: Claim 1 (as displayed): position sensor for the tip; electromagnetic circuit carrying a current and forming, in proportion to it, a magnetic force attracting the tip to the sensory surface; drive circuit varying the force by varying the current in dependence on a haptic-force signal.
limitations: Claims read from Google Patents text, not the USPTO image; not legal advice.
relevance_to_design: Close to the electromagnet options (i-b, ii); our recommended head uses a permanent magnet moved by a stage, not a current-proportional electromagnetic force
transferability_reason: Touch-screen framing; attorney to assess scope
design_implication: Freedom-to-operate review before any electromagnet head; the permanent-magnet head is a design-around candidate

topic: Passive guidance by steerable nonholonomic transmissions (cobots)

task_or_setup: Manipulator whose joints are coupled by variable (steerable) transmissions adjusted by small steering motors from a force sensor, implementing software virtual surfaces passively
key_quantitative_findings: Claim 1 (as summarised on Google Patents): manipulator with joints, variable transmission elements coupling the joint motions, small steering motors adjusting the ratios under computer control, a force sensor for operator intent, and a control computer implementing virtual surfaces; cobots are intrinsically passive (they steer motion that the person supplies).
limitations: Claim text from a summary display; expired.
relevance_to_design: Prior art (free to use) for a passive guidance principle: a steered wheel at the pen could guide using the paper as ground, without a board
design_implication: Future handheld idea only; not studied
